caption:
If you’re an  photocard collector or a newbie at collecting then you know that it can get expensive really quickly, especially for groups with a lot of members. Most albums come with different versions so once you do the math on that the price starts climbing.

Let’s use BTS and their latest release (Map of the Soul: Persona) as an example for today’s math lesson:

  • # of members: 7
  • # of versions: 4
  • average cost of album: $20 USD

So now we take the # of members x # of versions = 28 photocards (this is if you get a new photocard you don’t have with each purchase)

Now we take 28 photocards x $20 USD = $560 USD

note: this happening for someone is very slim so odds are you would buy multiple copies to try and complete the entire collection.

Some other options you have instead of buying the albums out right is to buy and/or trade photocards outright. Some of the most common places you will find this is:

  • Facebook Groups
  • Facebook Marketplace 
  • Instagram
  • Ebay
  • Mercari

I’ve added stars to the best and most reliable options, so let’s go through each one:

Facebook Groups⭐

Most Facebook groups of selling and trading photocards will be private but most are easy to be approved for. This is normally where I personally go and will look through the posts to see if anyone has a certain photocard I am missing so I’m not buying multiple albums trying to get it. Some things to know before you start buying:

  1. Expect to pay $5-$12 on average for a photocard (this depends on the seller and most will be willing to haggle with you, just don’t low ball them)
  2. Ask for proof that they have the card on hand by having them send you a picture of the card with their Facebook account name and the date.
  3. Always ask for proof of trade or sales in the past. Most sellers will gladly send you proof, now one thing to keep in mind is that there are some sellers that may be selling for the first time and don’t have proof. If this is a trade, then ask them to send their photocard first. If it’s their first time selling use the Goods and Services option instead of Family and Friends option.
  4. Ask for a picture or video of them dropping it off at the post office
  5. Most sellers use PayPal. When going through PayPal most will probably ask you to pay the Goods and Services (G&S) fees. The G&S fees are basically the tiny bit of money that PayPal takes is to allow you to use their services if you get scammed. If the seller never sends their item then you can get your money back. I use this G&S calculator to let me know what i need to add to the total (ex: photocards is $5 + $.46 G&S fee then i would pay the seller $5.46 which would have the payment they receive be $5)
  6. Some sellers ship worldwide but the shipping prices get very expensive so that is something to keep in mind.
  7. Ask them to show you your address on the envelope so you can double check that they have written your address down correctly.
  8. If you are spending more than $10 on a photocard then my advice is to ask for tracked shipping.
  9. Ask them to put the card in a top loader (or between two pieces of cardboard if they don’t have one) and a plastic bag in case of rain.
  10. Common acronyms used and their meanings: WTS (willing to sell), WTT (willing to trade), LFB (looking for buyer), LFS (looking for seller).

Facebook Marketplace⭐

Facebook Marketplace is like the Facebook Groups but you won’t have as much of a selection but they usually live closer to you and and that can sometimes save you on tracked shipping depending on what you buy (CD, DVD, Photocard, etc…). Facebook Marketplace is almost exactly like the Facebook Groups so a lot of the same advice is the same, but some things you should know before using the marketplace:

  1. Expect to pay $5-$12 on average for a photocard (this depends on the seller and most will be willing to haggle with you, just don’t low ball them)
  2. Ask for proof that they have the card on hand by having them send you a picture of the card with their Facebook account name and the date.
  3. Always ask for proof of trade or sales in the past. Most sellers will gladly send you proof, now one thing to keep in mind is that there are some sellers that may be selling for the first time and don’t have proof. If this is a trade, then ask them to send their photocard first. If it’s their first time selling use the Goods and Services option instead of Family and Friends option.
  4. Ask for a picture or video of them dropping it off at the post office
  5. Most sellers use PayPal. When going through PayPal most will probably ask you to pay the Goods and Services (G&S) fees. The G&S fees are basically the tiny bit of money that PayPal takes is to allow you to use their services if you get scammed. If the seller never sends their item then you can get your money back. I use this G&S calculator to let me know what i need to add to the total (ex: photocards is $5 + $.46 G&S fee then i would pay the seller $5.46 which would have the payment they receive be $5)
  6. Ask them to show you your address on the envelope so you can double check that they have written your address down correctly.
  7. If you are spending more than $10 on a photocard then my advice is to ask for tracked shipping.
  8. Ask them to put the card in a top loader (or between two pieces of cardboard if they don’t have one) and a plastic bag in case of rain.

Instagram⭐

I personally haven’t bought from Instagram but i know a lot of people who do. A lot of sellers in the Facebook Groups have Instagram which is where they keep a lot of their proof of sales and trades. It depends on the account you go to but some do actual auctions for a certain amount of time and some you just comment or DM them that you want to buy that item. A few of the same rules apply to this but here are some things you should know before buying from Instagram sellers:

  1. Ask for proof that they have the card on hand by having them send you a picture of the card with their Instagram account name and the date.
  2. Most will direct you to their stories or other posts with proof of trades and sales
  3. Ask for a picture or video of them dropping it off at the post office
  4. Most sellers use PayPal. When going through PayPal most will probably ask you to pay the Goods and Services (G&S) fees. The G&S fees are basically the tiny bit of money that PayPal takes is to allow you to use their services if you get scammed. If the seller never sends their item then you can get your money back. I use this G&S calculator to let me know what i need to add to the total (ex: photocards is $5 + $.46 G&S fee then i would pay the seller $5.46 which would have the payment they receive be $5)
  5. Some sellers ship worldwide but the shipping prices get very expensive so that is something to keep in mind.
  6. Ask them to show you your address on the envelope so you can double check that they have written your address down correctly.
  7. If you are spending more than $10 on a photocard then my advice is to ask for tracked shipping.
  8. Ask them to put the card in a top loader (or between two pieces of cardboard if they don’t have one) and a plastic bag in case of rain.
  9. Common acronyms used and their meanings: WTS (willing to sell), WTT (willing to trade).

Ebay

To be honest Ebay is one of those options that’s a hit or miss type deal. If you find some reputable sellers my advice would be to stick with that seller. A lot of people who get scammed with fake photocards that are unofficial happen on Ebay. Don’t get me wrong, there are some great sellers on Ebay and not everyone is out to scam you but it is definitely something you want to keep an eye out for, especially on Ebay. Here are some things you should know before buying on Ebay:

  1. Do your research before buying! A good option would be going on Reddit to r/kpopcollections or r/kpophelp subreddits and ask if anyone has some reputable sellers they would suggest buying from.  
  2. Make sure you look at the sellers reviews, good and bad.
  3. I Suggest checking out this post from Army Amino that talks about how to spot fake photocards (here is a good post on Army Amino that explains how to spot fake photocards).
  4. Message the seller and ask if they will send you a picture of the photocard, their ebay username, and the date.
  5. Look at shipping options (or ask them) and see if tracked shipping is available, if so, spend the extra money for tracked shipping.
  6. Try not to go with the first seller you see, shop around and see if you can find the same card for a better price (don’t sacrifice great seller ratings for a lower price).
  7. Try and find an estimate on shipping time, sometimes if you buy goods with photocards (CDs, DVDs, etc…) it can take longer to get to you.

Mercari

I’ve never bought from Mercari myself but it’s a lot like Ebay and Instagram had a baby. I’ve known people that have bought from it and had great experiences and some that haven’t. You still have the same type of risks that you do on Ebay but i would consider the risk to be much lower. Here are some things you should know before you buy on Mercari:

  1. I Suggest checking out this post from Army Amino that talks about how to spot fake photocards (here is a good post on Army Amino that explains how to spot fake photocards).
  2. Message the seller and ask if they will send you a picture of the photocard, their Mercari username, and the date.
  3. Look at shipping options (or ask them) and see if tracked shipping is available, if so, spend the extra money for tracked shipping.
  4. Try not to go with the first seller you see, shop around and see if you can find the same card for a better price.
  5. Ask for a picture or video of them dropping it off at the post office.
  6. Most sellers use PayPal. When going through PayPal most will probably ask you to pay the Goods and Services (G&S) fees. The G&S fees are basically the tiny bit of money that PayPal takes is to allow you to use their services if you get scammed. If the seller never sends their item then you can get your money back. I use this G&S calculator to let me know what i need to add to the total (ex: photocards is $5 + $.46 G&S fee then i would pay the seller $5.46 which would have the payment they receive be $5)
  7. Some sellers ship worldwide but the shipping prices get very expensive so that is something to keep in mind.
  8. Ask them to show you your address on the envelope so you can double check that they have written your address down correctly.
  9. If you are spending more than $10 on a photocard then my advice is to ask for tracked shipping.
  10. Ask them to put the card in a top loader (or between two pieces of cardboard if they don’t have one) and a plastic bag in case of rain.

All of the options listed above are only a few of the options you can find to buy and sell photocards. Those options are basically buying and trading from person to person, but what about buying from a company?

If you’re someone who enjoys getting everything else that comes with the albums and not just the photocards? Then i’m here to share my proven method that most people probably don’t know about…

think of Amazon Warehouse as an outlet store of sorts. When you go on Amazon to buy something a lot of times you will see the option to buy it used. Now most people think that this is probably people who are selling it that have already used it, especially when it comes to kpop albums, BUT i can attest to the fact that most likely isn’t the case.

A lot of Amazon Warehouse deals are the same products that may have cosmetic damage on it that doesn’t do any harm to the actual contents inside. I have yet to receive and album that didn’t have the photocard in it and I’ve bought many albums from there.

Here are the steps to find Amazon Warehouse deals:

  • You’ll want to go to the search bar and choose Amazon Warehouse from the drop down options and then type in kpop albums or whatever it is you’re looking for.
  • Next you will choose the album you’re wanting to buy and you will be taken to the screen below (Always read the conditions!).

    *note: if you have prime it makes these deals even sweeter
  • add it to your cart and check out and viola your album with everything is on your doorstep within days. I have yet to get any albums with extreme noticeable damage and some that look brand new.

Here are the steps to find Amazon Seller deals:

  • You’ll want to go to the search bar and then type in kpop albums or whatever it is you’re looking for and make sure to choose CDs & Vinyl from the drop down menu.
  • Go to the filters on the left side and choose Used
  • You’ll choose the album you want and it will take you to the sellers that are selling the album you’re looking for.


  • Make sure to note the shipping and estimated tax that will be added to the price that is listed (ex: $6.39)
  • Make sure to pay attention to the conditions of the items and read the entire description.
  • Also don’t ignore the seller information and make sure to look at their ratings and reviews.
  • Take note of the delivery time, majority of the sellers won’t be using prime so you will want to make sure that you’re aware of the shipping window. It’s rare for it to actually take that long but if it’s being shipped internationally it will take longer than normal.

I hope this post helps someone or at least gives you a little bit of information you may not have known. This post took over and hour to write because I wanted to try and cover as much as I could but still make it easy for anyone reading. I’ve thought about making a post on the best websites to get kpop albums from and the pros and cons of each, if that is something you would be interested in then let me know. Good look collecting!
